---
title: "Exercise 4.7"
---


## Solution
Define
$$E=(0,\epsilon)\cup\bigl(\mathbb Q\cap(\epsilon,1)\bigr).$$
Then $E\subset[0,1]$, and $E$ is measurable.

Since
$$\overline{(0,\epsilon)}=[0,\epsilon]$$
and $\mathbb Q\cap(\epsilon,1)$ is dense in $(\epsilon,1)$,
$$\overline{\mathbb Q\cap(\epsilon,1)}=[\epsilon,1].$$
Therefore,
$$\overline E=[0,1].$$


Moreover,
$$m\bigl(\mathbb Q\cap(\epsilon,1)\bigr)=0,$$
so
$$m(E) = m((0,\epsilon)) + m\bigl(\mathbb Q\cap(\epsilon,1)\bigr) = \epsilon.$$
